newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 6.

text.p: - Iraqi President Saddam Hussein has sought President Ramos' support in protesting against the U.S. missile attacks on his military installations in southern Iraq. Through his Charge d'Affaires Akmad Mansour, the Iraqi president condemned the attacks as "pure and simple form of aggression." (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)
- The Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) on Thursday vowed not to disrupt the September 9 elections in the Autonomous Region of Moslem Mindanao. (THE MANILA CHRONICLE)

- Immigration officials are looking at Davao, Subic, Laoag and Mactan international airports as possible entry points of terrorists out to sabotage the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit here. (TODAY)
- The health department confirmed on Thursday that the diarrhea cases which surged since last weekend in Manila's fifth district were caused by an outbreak of cholera. (TODAY)
- A bill has been filed in the House of Representatives calling for the total lifting of the ban on political advertisements in the media during elections. (THE PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Inflation in August fell to 7.9 percent from the previous month's 8.9 percent, recording the lowest rate since July last year. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The chairman of the Senate ways and means committee has assured prompt approval of the remaining components of the comprehensive tax reform package as soon as the Lower House wraps up deliberations on the unpopular tax measure. (THE BUSINESS DAILY)
